info.title: Mimiry Compute API
info.description:
GPU compute session management and billing API for the Mimiry platform.
Launch GPU-powered compute sessions, manage SSH access, and track billing.

## Authentication

Most endpoints require a JWT Bearer token obtained via SSH signature exchange
(`POST /api/auth/v1/token`) or portal login. The **GPU Availability** and
**GPU Catalog** endpoints are public and require no authentication.

## Sessions

Sessions have two dimensions:

- **`state`** (where the session is): `submitted` → `provisioned` →
  `booting` → `setting_up` → `pulling_image` → `running`. A session whose
  container has exited is `exited` (the outcome is in `exit_code`); one
  whose workload is over while its machine is kept is `idle`. Ending
  passes through `terminating` to `terminated`. A step that fails stops
  in `provision_failed`, `boot_failed`, `setup_failed`, `pull_failed` or
  `start_failed`. Every state except `terminated` and `provision_failed`
  has a machine behind it and is billed. Only a live session can be
  terminated: `submitted`, `provisioned`, `booting`, `boot_failed`,
  `setting_up`, `setup_failed`, `pulling_image`, `pull_failed`,
  `start_failed`, `running` and `idle`. Terminating any other answers
  `400 invalid_state`.
- **`operation`** (what is happening now): `provisioning`,
  `starting__setting_up`, `starting__pulling_image`,
  `starting__starting_container`, `stopping__stopping_container`,
  `terminating`. Absent when nothing is in progress.

SSH access is enabled by default. While a session is `running`, its SSH
connection details are included in the response.

## Billing

Sessions are billed per-GPU-hour from the authenticated user's credit
balance. All prices are in **EUR**. Check your balance before launching
sessions. Credits are added to your account by Mimiry.

Money is sent as JSON numbers, rounded where it leaves the platform:
amounts (balances, transactions, required funds) to the cent, and rates
(`hourly_rate`, `from_hourly_rate`, `rate_per_gb_hour`) to 6 decimal
places. Do arithmetic on them in decimal, not binary floating point.

## Async Operations

Creating or terminating a session, and creating, extending or deleting a
volume, return `202 Accepted` with an absolute `status_url`. Poll it for
the outcome.

## Errors

An error body is `{"error": "<code>", "message": "<text>"}`. The code is
lower-case and stable (`unauthorized`, `not_found`, `validation_failed`,
…); the message is for people and may change. Some errors add fields:
`validation_failed` lists `errors[]` of `{field, message}`, and
`insufficient_balance` and `quota_exceeded` carry their figures.

A `404` with a JSON body means the resource was not found. A path or method
that does not exist answers `404` with the plain-text body
`404 page not found` once you are signed in, and `401` before.

tags.description: Check GPU availability and pricing before launching sessions.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description: Create and manage GPU compute sessions.

tags.name: Volumes
tags.description:
Persistent block volumes scoped per organization. Volumes survive
across sessions — attaching a volume to a session is non-destructive,
and the volume detaches (not deletes) when the session ends.

get.description:
Returns the GPU catalog — technical specifications for all known GPU
models.

**No authentication required.**

### Example

```bash
curl "https://api.example.com/api/compute/v1/catalog"
```

Returns availability, pricing and locations for GPU models.

**No authentication required.** This endpoint is public and returns
no user-specific data. Offerings are refreshed by the platform on its
own schedule; a request never triggers a fresh lookup.

### Filters

A filter sent with no value (`?min_hourly_rate=`, `?location=`) is
rejected with **400** naming the parameter. Leave a filter out to apply
no filter.

### Pricing

All prices are in **EUR** and include the platform margin. The
`providers` array on each GPU model holds one pricing summary: the
model's cheapest rate and the locations where it is in stock.

For the price of a specific machine shape, read `skus[].listings[]`.
With the default `available_only=true` it holds only purchasable
listings; with `available_only=false` it also holds listings with
`available: false`.

### Locations

A location is our location code: the country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and a
number, such as `FI-1`. A code always means the same place. Use it in
the `location` filter, in `gpu.location` when creating a session, and in
`location` when creating a volume.

### Use cases
- Pre-flight check before creating a session
- Status dashboard showing which GPU types are available
- CLI tooling to select the best GPU type

### Examples

```bash
# All available GPUs (summary)
curl "https://api.example.com/api/compute/v1/availability"

# Filter by family, include unavailable, full details
curl "https://api.example.com/api/compute/v1/availability?gpu_family=H100&available_only=false&detail=full"

# Minimum VRAM filter
curl "https://api.example.com/api/compute/v1/availability?min_vram_gb=40"
```

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Not accepted: the platform does not name the companies it buys
capacity from. Sending it is refused with **400**. Filter by
`location` instead.

parameters.name: gpu_family
parameters.description: Filter by GPU family. Comma-separated for multiple families.

parameters.name: form_factor
parameters.description: Filter by form factor. Comma-separated for multiple values.

parameters.name: min_vram_gb
parameters.description:
Minimum VRAM in GB. A value that is not a non-negative integer is
currently treated as 0 (no filter) rather than refused.

parameters.name: min_gpu_count
parameters.description:
Minimum GPU count per configuration. A value that is not a
non-negative integer is currently treated as 0 (no filter) rather
than refused.

parameters.name: min_hourly_rate
parameters.description:
Only listings priced at or above this hourly rate (EUR, post-margin).
Inclusive.

parameters.name: max_hourly_rate
parameters.description:
Only listings priced at or below this hourly rate (EUR, post-margin).
Inclusive.

**These two filter `skus[].listings[]`, not `providers[].hourly_rate`.**
A model's headline rate is the cheapest listing we know of, and it is
not necessarily one that can be bought: on 2026-09-30
`RTX_96G_PCIe` advertised EUR 1.3624 — a variant with no stock — while
its only in-stock listing cost EUR 2.4590. A price filter has to read
the unit that gets transacted, so it reads the listing. A model with
no listing left inside the band is omitted from the response
entirely rather than returned with an empty `skus[]`.

🚨 `providers[].hourly_rate` is NOT narrowed by the band, so it can
sit below `min_hourly_rate`. That is not a contradiction: it is the
catalogue's cheapest known rate for the model, band or no band.
Read `skus[].listings[].hourly_rate` for what you can buy.

A value that cannot be parsed, a negative value, or a
`min_hourly_rate` above `max_hourly_rate` returns **400**, never an
empty list — "nothing is available in your budget" and "your filter
could not be applied" are different answers and must not look alike.

The same two names are accepted on session create as
`gpu.min_hourly_rate` / `gpu.max_hourly_rate`, so a band you can
browse is a band you can buy in.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
Only offerings at this location code (e.g. `FI-1`). Any other value is
refused with **400** `invalid_location`, naming the codes.

parameters.name: available_only
parameters.description:
Show only available GPUs and purchasable listings. Only the exact
value `true` (the default when omitted) keeps the filter; any other
value turns it off.

parameters.name: include_cpu
parameters.description:
Include machines with no GPU. Only the exact value `true` includes
them.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description:
Response detail level (any value other than `full` means `summary`):
- `summary` — `name`, `display_name`, `family`, `vram_gb`,
  `available`, `currency`, `providers` and `skus`
- `full` — adds `form_factor`, `fp16_tflops`, `configurations` and
  `price_updated_at`

400.description:
A filter that could not be applied: a filter sent with no value, an
unparseable or negative rate, or `min_hourly_rate` above
`max_hourly_rate`.

example.message: min_hourly_rate (3) is above max_hourly_rate (2), so no listing can match

503.description:
The platform's offerings could not be read. (When prices alone are
unavailable the answer is currently `200` with `gpu_models: null`,
not this; treat a `null` list as "could not tell", not as "nothing
available".)

example.message: Unable to fetch availability data. Try again later.

post.description:
Launches a new GPU compute session. The session is provisioned
asynchronously — poll `GET /api/compute/v1/sessions/{id}` for status.

### Defaults
- `ssh_enabled`: `true`
- `auto_terminate`: `true` (terminates when command completes)
- `result_storage`: `"script_managed"`

### Billing
Sessions are always billed to the authenticated user's personal credit
balance. Requires sufficient credit balance (EUR). Returns `402` if
balance is insufficient or no billing account exists.

### Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/compute/v1/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "training-run",
    "image": {"uri": "nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.01-py3"},
    "gpu": {"types": ["H100_80G_SXM"], "count": 1},
    "ssh_public_key": "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... user@host"
  }'
```

400.description:
The request was refused before anything was created. Checks run in
this order: the body is read (`invalid_request`), validated
(`validation_failed`, every problem listed in `errors[]`), the
organisation is resolved (`no_organization`,
`ambiguous_organization`, only with `volume_mounts` and no
`org_id`), and the SSH key is checked (`invalid_ssh_key`).

errors.message: image URI must be from an allowed registry

value.message: You belong to 2 organizations — pass org_id explicitly when mounting volumes. Available: 7d0f1c2e-5a8b-4c3d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f, 0b1c2d3e-4f5a-6b7c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
SSH key not found or doesn't belong to user

402.description: Insufficient credits or no billing account.

value.message: Insufficient balance to start job (need €10.00, have €2.50)
No billing account found. Contact support to add credits.

404.description: An `org_id` was given that is not one of the caller's organisations.

409.description:
No machine can take the session now (`gpu_unavailable`), or the
organisation is not accepting new work (`org_not_found`,
`org_winding_down`, `org_retired`, `org_not_accepting`).

value.message: No machine matches type H100_80G_SXM. Run 'mimiry availability' to see what is available.
This organization is winding down and cannot take on new members, invitations or resources. Cancel the wind-down if it was started in error, or create the resource under another organization.

429.description:
A quota is reached. `limit` names it: `max_concurrent_sessions`,
`max_gpu_hours_daily` or `max_gpu_hours_monthly`. `resets_at` is
`null` for the concurrent limit.

503.description:
Prices (`pricing_unavailable`) or the organisation's status
(`org_admission_unavailable`) could not be read. Nothing was
created; retry shortly.

example.message: GPU pricing temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.

get.description:
Returns all compute sessions for the authenticated user.
Events are omitted from list responses — use `GET /sessions/{id}`
for event details.

### Filtering

- `state` / `state_not` — comma-separated lists of session states.
  A single value (`?state=running`) is parsed as a one-element
  inclusion list.
- `operation` / `operation_not` — comma-separated lists of primary
  operation values (provisioning, starting, stopping, terminating).
  The backend prefix-matches against compound values, so
  `?operation=starting` covers `starting__setting_up`,
  `starting__pulling_image`, and `starting__starting_container`.
  Empty string is a valid token (filters resting sessions).
- `updated_after` / `updated_before` — RFC 3339 timestamps bounding
  the last *durable state change*. `updated_after` is inclusive,
  `updated_before` is exclusive. Either bound is optional. To
  express "updated on date D", pass `updated_after=D` and
  `updated_before=D+1day` — no rounding ambiguity.
- `org_id` — sessions attributed to that organisation. An organisation
  you are not in, or a value matching nothing, gives an empty list.

All filters are AND-combined. An invalid state, operation or timestamp
returns `400 invalid_filter`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Inclusion filter — keep sessions whose state is in this comma-separated list.

parameters.name: state_not
parameters.description: Exclusion filter — drop sessions whose state is in this comma-separated list.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description:
Inclusion filter on the primary operation (e.g. `starting`).
Backend prefix-matches against compound values, so `starting`
covers `starting__setting_up`, `starting__pulling_image`, and
`starting__starting_container`.

parameters.name: operation_not
parameters.description: Exclusion filter on the primary operation. Same prefix-match semantics.

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Lower bound (inclusive) on the session's last durable state-change timestamp.

parameters.name: updated_before
parameters.description: Upper bound (exclusive) on the session's last durable state-change timestamp.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Keep sessions attributed to this organisation.

get.description:
Returns details for a specific session including status and SSH
connection info (when running).

### SSH Access

While a session is `running` and has `ssh_enabled: true`, the
response includes SSH connection details:

```json
{
  "ssh": {
    "host": "gpu-node-1.compute.mimiry.com",
    "port": 22,
    "username": "user"
  }
}
```

parameters.name: events_tail
parameters.description:
Number of events to include (newest first). Default `3`. Any
negative value (such as `-1`) includes all events; `0`, none. A value
that is not an integer means `3`. `events_total` always shows the
total count regardless of this parameter.

delete.description:
Terminates a live session: `submitted`, `provisioned`, `booting`,
`boot_failed`, `setting_up`, `setup_failed`, `pulling_image`,
`pull_failed`, `start_failed`, `running` or `idle`. An `idle` session
still holds its machine and is billed, so terminate it when you are done.
Returns `202 Accepted`; the termination is processed asynchronously.

400.description: The session is not live (`exited`, `terminating`, `terminated` or `provision_failed`).

get.description:
Returns a session's log lines: the container's output and the
platform's messages about the session, read from the log store.

Available in every state, including after the session has ended, for
as long as the lines are retained. A session that has only just
started may return no lines yet.

### Retries
If the log store cannot be reached, returns `503` with
`retry_after_seconds`. Retry after the indicated interval.

### Example

```bash
curl "https://api.example.com/api/compute/v1/sessions/{id}/logs?tail=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description:
Number of most recent lines to return. A value above 5000 means
5000; a value that is not a positive integer means 100.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Start of the window: an RFC 3339 timestamp, or a duration back from
now in hours, minutes or seconds (`30m`, `24h`, `1h30m`). Defaults
to the last 24 hours. A value that is neither — including days, such
as `7d` — currently also means the last 24 hours rather than being
refused.

parameters.name: timestamps
parameters.description: Accepted for compatibility; has no effect.

503.description:
The log store could not be read. Retry after `retry_after_seconds`.
When the field is absent, this instance has no log store and
retrying will not help.

example.message: Log store temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.

get.summary: Get a session's live machine metrics
get.description:
The latest metrics the session's machine reported: GPU utilisation,
memory, temperature and power, host memory, and the container's status.
The machine reports every 30 seconds while it runs, and a report is kept
for 2 minutes. `age_seconds` says how old this one is.

Only the machine's first GPU is reported; on a multi-GPU machine the GPU
figures are GPU 0's.

A session with no report in the last 2 minutes — not yet running, ended,
or not reporting — answers `404 no_health_data`.

404.description:
The session does not exist or is not yours (`not_found`), or there
is no report from its machine in the last 2 minutes
(`no_health_data`).

example.message: No health data available for this session

get.description:
Returns current quota usage and limits for the authenticated user. A
limit of `0` means unlimited.

Returns the credit balance for the authenticated user's personal
billing account. All amounts are in EUR. A caller with no billing
account yet gets every amount `0` and `active_sessions: null`.

get.summary: Get an organization's balance (requires elevated rights)
get.description:
Returns the credit balance for an organization. Requires membership
in the organization: a UUID you are not a member of answers `403`,
whether or not the organisation exists.

An organisation with no billing account of its own bills the account
that agreed to pay for it. Only that payer is shown those figures;
any other member reads a zero balance.

parameters.name: id_or_slug
parameters.description: Organization ID (UUID) or slug.

404.description: A slug that names no organisation.

get.description:
Returns billing transaction history for the authenticated user,
sorted newest-first. Paginate with `limit` / `offset` per the
platform list-response convention.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Keep rows created at or after this RFC 3339 time (inclusive).

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Keep rows created before this RFC 3339 time (exclusive).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Keep only credits or only debits.

parameters.name: resource_id
parameters.description:
Keep the rows that charged one session or volume. A resource that
is not yours, or unknown, gives an empty page.

post.description:
Creates a new persistent block volume. The owning organization is
specified by `org_id` in the request body — the caller must be a
member of that organization. `org_id` may be left out when the caller
belongs to exactly one organization.

Volume names are unique within the organization, and stay reserved
after a volume is deleted. A taken name is not refused here: the
request is accepted (`202`) and the volume then ends `failed`, with a
`reason` naming the clash.

The volume is provisioned asynchronously — poll
`GET /api/compute/v1/volumes/{volume_id}` for status.

### Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/compute/v1/volumes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"org_id": "<uuid>", "name": "training-data", "size_gb": 100, "volume_type": "nvme"}'
```

400.description:
The body could not be read or failed a basic check
(`invalid_request`: a size outside 100–10000 GB, a `volume_type`
other than `nvme` or `hdd`), the `location` is not one volumes can
be created in (`invalid_location`), or no `org_id` was given and the
caller belongs to none or several organizations
(`no_organization`, `ambiguous_organization`).

404.description: The organization does not exist or the caller is not a member.

409.description:
The organization is not accepting new resources (`org_not_found`,
`org_winding_down`, `org_retired`, `org_not_accepting`).

503.description: The organization's status could not be read (`org_admission_unavailable`). Retry shortly.

get.description:
Returns all volumes the caller has access to (across every
organization the user is a member of). Filtering mirrors the
sessions API — see `GET /sessions` for full semantics.

- `org_id` — narrow to one organization the user belongs to. An
  organization you are not in gives an empty list.
- `attached` — `true` keeps volumes attached to a session, `false`
  those that are not. Any other value is refused.
- `state` / `state_not` — comma-separated lists of volume states.
- `operation` / `operation_not` — primary operation values
  (provisioning, resizing, deleting). Prefix-matches compound
  values, so `?operation=deleting` covers both
  `deleting__detaching_volume` and `deleting__deleting_volume`.
- `updated_after` / `updated_before` — half-open RFC 3339
  interval `[after, before)` on the last *durable state change*.

AND across all params. An invalid value returns `400 invalid_filter`.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Optional filter — limit results to one organization.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Inclusion filter — keep volumes whose state is in this comma-separated list.

parameters.name: state_not
parameters.description: Exclusion filter — drop volumes whose state is in this comma-separated list.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description:
Inclusion filter on the primary operation (e.g. `deleting`).
Backend prefix-matches against compound values, so `deleting`
covers `deleting__detaching_volume` and `deleting__deleting_volume`.

parameters.name: operation_not
parameters.description: Exclusion filter on the primary operation. Same prefix-match semantics.

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Lower bound (inclusive) on the volume's last durable state-change timestamp.

parameters.name: updated_before
parameters.description: Upper bound (exclusive) on the volume's last durable state-change timestamp.

parameters.name: attached
parameters.description: Keep attached volumes (`true`) or unattached ones (`false`).

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a volume. A volume attached to a session is
detached first and then deleted: its `operation` moves through
`deleting__detaching_volume` to `deleting__deleting_volume`, and it ends
in state `deleted`. Deleting a volume already being deleted is
accepted again.

Deletion is asynchronous; poll the volume until its state is `deleted`.

patch.description:
Increases the size of a volume to `size_gb`. Shrinking is not supported.
Extension is asynchronous: the volume's `operation` is `resizing` while
it runs, and its state stays `provisioned` throughout.

400.description: The new size is not larger than the current one, or outside 100–10000 GB.

example.message: New size (100 GB) must be larger than current size (200 GB)

bearerAuth.description:
JWT token obtained via SSH signature exchange (`POST /api/auth/v1/token`)
or portal login (`POST /api/auth/v1/login`).

Include in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description:
Maximum number of items to return, 1 to 100. A value above 100 means
100; a value that is not a positive integer means 50.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description:
Number of items to skip. A value that is not a non-negative integer
means 0.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be read, or a field failed a basic check.

InvalidFilter.description: A list filter could not be applied. The message names it.

Forbidden.description: The caller may not read this resource.

example.message: You must be a member of this organization to view its balance

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or is not the caller's.

InternalError.description: An unexpected failure on the platform's side. Retry later.

SessionState.description: Durable lifecycle stage of a session. See the Sessions section of the overview.

SessionOperation.description:
Transient indicator of the in-progress activity on a session.
Format: `<primary>` or `<primary>__<sub_step>`. Empty when the
session is at a durable resting state.

SessionOperationPrimary.description:
Primary (top-level) activity portion of `SessionOperation`.
Used in `?operation=` query filters — backend prefix-matches
compound values from the same family.

VolumeState.description: Durable lifecycle stage of a block volume.

VolumeOperation.description:
Transient indicator of the in-progress activity on a volume.
Format and rules mirror `SessionOperation`.

VolumeOperationPrimary.description: Primary activity portion of `VolumeOperation`. Used in `?operation=` query filters.

architectures.description:
The silicon generations this MODEL spans, as SKU tokens, oldest
first. Always present; never null.

Plural because a canonical model is not one machine:
`RTX_48G_PCIe` is served by an RTX A6000 (AMPERE) and an RTX 6000
Ada (ADA), which is why the generation is part of the SKU. Use
`/availability` when you need the architecture of a specific
machine — there it is a single value per SKU.

Empty means we have no generation to report: either the model has
no GPU (`vram_gb` is 0) or no live machine of it carried an
architecture we recognise.

gpu_models.description:
The matching GPU models. Currently `null`, not `[]`, when nothing
matches — and also when prices could not be read, so treat `null`
as "could not tell" rather than "nothing available".

GPUModelAvailability.description:
Availability and pricing for a GPU model. When `detail=full` is
requested, additional fields are included (form_factor, fp16_tflops,
price_updated_at, configurations).

Architecture is NOT one of them, and its absence is deliberate: a
model is a product family, so the generation belongs to the SKU
beneath it, not to the model. `detail=full` carried a model-level
`architecture` until 2026-08-28; it was removed because it was incomplete
and disagreed with the SKUs beneath it.

available.description: Whether the GPU is currently available at one location or more.

providers.description:
The model's pricing summary: one entry, with the cheapest rate and
every location in stock. An entry with `available: false` is a price
we cannot serve at this moment — see ProviderPrice.available.

skus.description:
The machine shapes this model is sold in, sorted by `sku`. Present
in both detail levels; never null.

price_updated_at.description: When pricing was last refreshed. Only in `detail=full`.

SKU.description: One buyable machine shape of a model, and where it is offered.

sku.description:
The machine's identity: canonical name, an architecture segment for
families that span generations, then GPU count (`X`), vCPUs (`V`)
and memory in GB (`M`), and `_CC` when confidential.

confidential.description: Present and `true` for a confidential-computing machine.

from_hourly_rate.description: The cheapest listing's hourly rate, in `currency`.

listings.description: Where the shape is offered, sorted by `hourly_rate`.

instance_type.description: Not sent. The machine is identified by its SKU.

hourly_rate.description: The model's cheapest rate in EUR, among locations in stock when there are any.

locations.description:
Location codes where the model **currently has stock**. Empty when
`available` is false.

available.description:
Whether this GPU can be started **right now**.

An entry can carry a rate and `available: false`: the rate comes from
our price catalogue, which is refreshed on a slower cycle than stock.
So it means "we sell this, not at this moment" — a real price, and
not one you can buy today.

Since 2026-09-29. Absent from older responses; treat a missing field
as unknown rather than as false.

name.description:
Session display name: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting and
ending with a letter or digit.

org_id.description:
Organization the session is attributed to; it must be one of yours
(otherwise `404 not_found`), and the organization must be accepting
new work. Billing is always the caller's own account. When omitted,
a session with `volume_mounts` takes the caller's only organization
(`400 no_organization` with none, `400 ambiguous_organization` with
several); one without stays personal.

uri.description:
Container image URI. It must start with an allowed registry —
`nvcr.io/`, `docker.io/`, `ghcr.io/`, `gcr.io/` or `quay.io/` —
or be a Docker Hub short form whose first segment has no `.`
(`nvidia/cuda:12.3.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04`). A bare name with no
`/` (`ubuntu:22.04`) is refused.

gpu.description:
Selects the machine. At least one of `types`, `family`, `vram_gb`,
`form_factor`, `architecture`, a vCPU or memory bound, `max_vram_gb`,
`max_gpu_count` or `priority` is required; the price bounds alone
are not a selection.

types.description:
Acceptable GPU types, as canonical names from `/catalog` or
`/availability` (case-sensitive).

family.description: Acceptable GPU families, in preference order (e.g. `H100`).

vram_gb.description: Acceptable VRAM sizes in GB; the smallest is the VRAM floor.

count.description:
Minimum number of GPUs on the machine. For an exact count, also
set `max_gpu_count` to the same value.

max_gpu_count.description: Maximum number of GPUs on the machine; not below `count`.

max_vram_gb.description: Maximum VRAM in GB; not below the smallest `vram_gb`.

max_vcpus.description: Maximum vCPUs on the machine; not below `min_vcpus`.

priority.description:
How candidates are ordered. Every key but `PRICE` needs its
selector set (`GPU` → `types`, `FAMILY` → `family`,
`FORM_FACTOR` → `form_factor`, `VRAM` → `vram_gb`, `ARCH` →
`architecture`). Default: `["GPU"]` for a request with only
`types`, otherwise `["PRICE"]`.

max_attempts.description:
How many candidate machines to try before giving up. Absent, or
0 or less, means 3.

provider.description: Not accepted: the platform does not name the companies it buys capacity from. Sending it is refused with 400. Choose a `location` instead.

location.description: The location code to run in (see /availability, Locations). Any other value is refused with 400 `invalid_location`. A session that mounts volumes runs where they are.

min_memory_gb.description: Minimum host RAM in GB. Machines with less are not selected.

max_memory_gb.description: Maximum host RAM in GB. Machines with more are not selected.

min_hourly_rate.description:
Price floor (EUR, post-margin, per hour). Candidates priced below
it are not selected. Inclusive.

max_hourly_rate.description:
Price ceiling (EUR, post-margin, per hour). Candidates priced
above it are not selected. Inclusive.

These are the same two names `/availability` accepts as query
parameters, and they mean the same thing, so a band you browsed
is a band you can provision in.

🚨 **The affordability check follows the band.** The gate demands
one hour of balance against the cheapest machine the request can
be filled by, so a floor raises the amount required — it has to,
or you would be approved on a machine the selector is not
permitted to pick.

A negative value, or `min_hourly_rate` above `max_hourly_rate`,
is rejected with **400**. An impossible band that returned
"no capacity" would blame the market for a typo.

There is no exact form. Rates are post-margin values derived from
an FX conversion, so an equality filter would match nothing the
moment the last decimal moved; pass a narrow band instead.

min_gb.description:
Minimum host RAM in GB. Used as `gpu.min_memory_gb` when that
field is not given; when both are given, `gpu.min_memory_gb`
wins. Prefer `gpu.min_memory_gb` / `gpu.max_memory_gb`.

command.description: Command to run in the session.

environment_vars.description:
Environment variables. A name containing `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or
`TOKEN`, in any case, is refused.

ssh_enabled.description: Enable SSH access to the session.

ssh_key_id.description:
ID of an SSH key registered to your account. Keys are registered in
the portal; give `ssh_public_key` instead to use a key that is not.

ssh_public_key.description: SSH public key for session access. Required when `ssh_enabled: true` and no `ssh_key_id` is provided. Accepts any OpenSSH public key format (e.g., `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... user@host`).

auto_terminate.description:
Auto-terminate behavior. Accepts `true` (= `on_complete`),
`false` (= `never`), or an object `{"mode": "on_complete"|"on_success"|"never", "timeout_seconds": 0}`.
Default: `true`.

max_duration.description:
Longest the session may live, in seconds, counted from its start
(or creation, before it starts). Absent, or 0 or less, means the
platform default of 24 hours. When `auto_terminate.timeout_seconds`
is also set, the shorter of the two applies.

result_storage.description: How session results are stored. Currently only script_managed is supported.

volume_mounts.description:
Persistent block volumes to attach to this session. Volumes must
already exist in the session's organization (create them via
`POST /api/compute/v1/volumes` first). Volumes detach (not delete)
when the session ends. A volume, and a mount path, may appear once.

org_id.description: The organization the session is attributed to; absent for a personal session.

updated_at.description:
Last durable state-change timestamp. Bumped only on transitions
of `state` (submitted → provisioned, running → exited, etc.) —
NOT on transient `operation` flips, billing checkpoints, or
event-log appends. Use with `?updated_after=` / `?updated_before=`
on the list endpoint to find sessions changed in a given window.

ssh.description: SSH connection details (only when running and SSH enabled).

auto_terminate.description: Auto-terminate configuration, always an object here.

timeout_seconds.description: Timeout in seconds; absent means the server default.

exit_code.description: Container exit code (set after container exits).

stop_reason.description: Why the session was halted by an external force before it finished. Absent when the workload finished by itself — a session that ran to completion, or whose container exited on its own, is not "stopped" and carries no stop reason. `vendor_instance_gone` means the machine was gone and the platform released the session; `system_error` means the platform stopped it after a failure on our side.

events.description:
Session timeline events (newest first). Controlled by `events_tail`
query param. Omitted from list endpoint.

events_total.description: Total number of events available. Use `events_tail=-1` to fetch all.

billing.description:
What this session costs. Every phase is billed: provisioning, boot,
image pull and running. The machine is held for you, and paid for,
from the moment it is created, so billing starts at
`billed_from`, not at `started_at` (the container start). A session
that never got a machine is not billed. A minimum charge per session
may apply, so `final_cost` can exceed `duration_seconds` ×
`hourly_rate`.

hourly_rate.description: Rate in `currency` per hour, fixed when the machine is chosen.

billed_from.description:
When billing started: the moment the machine was created. Absent until a machine exists, and on sessions
recorded before 2026-10-27.

running_cost.description:
While the session is live, the cost so far: the time since
`billed_from` at `hourly_rate`. An estimate; `final_cost` is the
amount charged.

duration_seconds.description:
While the session is live, the seconds since `billed_from`.
Once it has ended, the duration it was billed for.

final_cost.description:
The amount charged for the session, set when it ends. Equal to
the sum of its charges in the transaction history.

committed_total.description: What has been charged so far, at the billing checkpoints passed.

reserved_amount.description: Credit currently held for this session against your balance.

SessionListResponse.description:
Canonical list-response shape — see API-CONVENTIONS-LIST.md.
`sessions` is always present and never null (empty list is `[]`).
`total_count` is the total before pagination; `limit`/`offset`
reflect the applied pagination.

unavailable.description:
Sessions that exist but could not be read on this request; they are
missing from `sessions` and from `total_count`. `0` when the page is
complete.

status.description:
`pending` (session create), `terminating` (session terminate),
`creating`, `deleting` or `extending` (volume create, delete,
extend).

status_url.description: Absolute URL of the resource to poll for the outcome.

container_status.description: The container's status as Docker reports it (`running`, `exited`, …), or `unknown`.

received_at.description: When the platform received this report.

max_concurrent_sessions.description: The most sessions that may be live at once. `0` means no limit.

max_gpu_hours_daily.description: The most GPU hours a day. `0` means no limit.

max_gpu_hours_monthly.description: The most GPU hours a month. `0` means no limit.

last_daily_reset.description: When the daily usage was last reset; `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` when not known.

last_monthly_reset.description: When the monthly usage was last reset; `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` when not known.

reserved.description: Credit held against running sessions and volumes.

available.description: `balance` minus `reserved`: what new work can draw on.

estimated_balance.description: Balance minus estimated running session costs.

active_sessions.description:
Sessions billed to this account that are still running or holding
a machine. `null` when the platform could not count them on this
read, which is not the same as `0`.

account_kind.description: `test` on an account used for automated testing; absent on an ordinary account.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 code denominating `amount` and `balance_after`. Always EUR
today. Read it rather than assuming it: an assumption baked into every
consumer is expensive to unpick on the day it stops holding.

resource_id.description:
The session or volume this row charged. Absent for deposits, which
charge no resource.

resource_type.description:
What `resource_id` refers to. `none` means the row charges no
resource by nature (a deposit); an ABSENT value means the row was
never classified, which is a different answer from `none` and must
not be rendered as one.

logs.description:
Log lines, oldest first, one per line: a UTC timestamp with
milliseconds, the origin in brackets (`[session]`, `[instance]` or
`[container]`, with `:warn` or `:error` appended for those
severities), then the message.

truncated.description: `true` when as many lines as `tail` were returned, so older lines may exist.

lines_requested.description: The `tail` value used for the request.

retry_after_seconds.description: Suggested number of seconds to wait before retrying.

resets_at.description: When the limit resets; `null` for the concurrent-session limit.

gpu_types.description: The `gpu.types` that were asked for, when there were any.

errors.description: Every problem found, not just the first.

message.example: image URI must be from an allowed registry

org_id.description:
Owning organization. **Optional**: if omitted, the server uses
the caller's only organization. Returns `400 no_organization`
if the caller belongs to none, or `400 ambiguous_organization`
(with the candidate org IDs in the message) if they belong to
more than one. When supplied explicitly, the caller must be a
member.

name.description:
Volume name, unique within the organization and still reserved
after the volume is deleted (a clash fails the volume; see the
create operation).

volume_type.description: Storage class. NVMe is faster; HDD is cheaper.

location.description:
The location code to create the volume at (see /availability,
Locations). A session can only mount a volume at its own location,
so set this when the volume is for a session. Omit it to accept the
default. A code that is not ours, or a location that does not offer
volumes, is refused with `400 invalid_location`, naming the codes that
do.

size_gb.description:
New size in gigabytes. Must be larger than the current size —
shrinking is not supported.

volume_name.description: Name of an existing volume in the user's organization.

mount_path.description:
Absolute path inside the container where the volume is mounted.
It must already be in clean form (no trailing `/`, no `//`, no `.`
or `..` segments), and may not be exactly one of `/`, `/bin`,
`/boot`, `/dev`, `/etc`, `/lib`, `/proc`, `/root`, `/sbin`, `/sys`,
`/usr`, `/var` or `/opt/mimiry` (paths beneath them are allowed).

VolumeResponse.description:
A persistent block volume. The platform is strictly state-driven:
- `state` is what the volume IS (durable lifecycle stage).
- `operation` is what's HAPPENING right now (transient activity).
- `attached_to` is a property/relationship, NOT a state — an
  attached volume is `state=provisioned, attached_to=<session_id>`.

After deletion the record is preserved with `state: "deleted"` so
direct GETs by id still return the last-known data. List endpoints
exclude deleted volumes.

attached_to.description:
Session ID this volume is currently attached to, or omitted
when detached. Independent of `state` — an attached volume is
still `state=provisioned`. On volume delete, this field drives
an automatic detach before destruction.

rate_per_gb_hour.description: Hourly billing rate per GB in EUR.

created_by.description: The user who created the volume; absent on volumes created before 2026-08-10.

updated_at.description:
Last durable state-change timestamp. Bumped only on transitions
of `state` (submitted → provisioned, provisioned → deleted, etc.)
— NOT on `operation` changes (`resizing`, `deleting__…`),
`attached_to` changes, billing checkpoints, or size changes. Use
with `?updated_after=` / `?updated_before=` on the list endpoint.

reason.description: Why the volume failed; present only when `state` is `failed`.

unavailable.description:
Volumes that exist but could not be read on this request; they are
missing from `volumes` and from `total_count`. `0` when the page is
complete.

ErrorResponse.description:
Every error from the public API has this shape. Branch on `error`, never on
`message`: the code is part of the API, while the sentence may be reworded.
Some errors carry more fields beside these two; each operation documents
its own.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence a person can read.
